question_stem: Nuclei of an isotope of samarium (Sm) each contain 62 protons and 85 neutrons.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the nuclide notation in the form $^{A}_{Z}X$ for this isotope of samarium.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Explain how Fig. 6.1 shows that this isotope of samarium emits $\alpha$-particles and does **not** emit $\beta$-particles.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
This isotope of samarium decays to an isotope of neodymium (Nd).

Give the radioactive decay equation for this decay. Include the nucleon and proton numbers of **all** the particles involved.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.part_stem:
A baryon is composed of three quarks which all have different flavours. The baryon has a charge of 0.

Two of the quarks in the baryon are an up quark and a bottom quark.
parts.text: Determine, in terms of the elementary charge $e$, the charge on the third quark in the baryon.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State a possible flavour for the third quark in the baryon.
